segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You and Pip climb down the stone steps beneath the frozen mill.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At the bottom is a hidden subterranean chamber carved out of solid river bedrock. The ceiling is reinforced with massive, frost-covered oak beams. Through thick blocks of green river ice set into the walls, you can see frozen fish suspended motionless in the current.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In the center of the chamber sits an ancient, heavy oak workbench.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: It is covered in delicate, gleaming tools: brass tweezers, magnifying lenses, miniature anvils, and racks of tiny glass vials filled with glowing, swirling purple liquid—the exact same color as the Cheer Hearth in Arizona!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip creeps up to the table, his nose twitching.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Good heavens. Someone has been modifying Everfrost's clockwork down here. In secret.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You walk around the bench. Resting in the center of the desk is a thick, leather-bound journal bound with tarnished silver clasps. On the front cover, two ornate letters are stamped in worn gold foil:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: C. M.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: Pip,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you whisper.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: Whose journal is this?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip steps up beside you on his tiptoes. With trembling paws, he unclasps the silver latch and opens to the final, yellowed page. The handwriting is sharp, precise, and filled with deep, jagged ink strokes:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: December 24, 1842.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Santa receives the songs, the children's laughter, the warm hearths, and the world's adoration. And what am I? I am the Clockmaker. The man in the grease and shadows. The forgotten architect who keeps his great machine from tearing the world apart.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: No more.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: If humanity loves his Christmas so dearly, I shall give it to them forever. The Great Clock will turn back the hours, unspooling yesterday, until every season, every memory, and every ordinary day is swallowed by the frost.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They will finally remember who gave them eternity.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: — C.M.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Silence fills the cold vault.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip’s jaw dropped open. His paws shook so hard the pages of the journal fluttered.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Santa... Santa had a partner?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip whispered, his accent completely gone in sheer disbelief.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: The Clockmaker... he didn't just sabotage the clock. He built it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Before you can answer, the stone floor violently trembles!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: BOOOOOM.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Deep within the riverbed, the iron drive-shaft groans. Up above, the distant Grand Clock chimes its next backwards hour.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: BONG.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Twelve.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A warning bell begins to clang on the workbench. A small brass speaker horn crackles to life on the wall, and a familiar, overly cheerful wooden voice echoes through the room:

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: VAULT TAMPERING DETECTED AT SUB-SECTOR WATERMILL. DISPATCHING NUTCRACKER SPECIAL CONTINGENT.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip snaps the journal shut and shoves it into his coat. He looks up at you with wide, frantic eyes.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: We need to move,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip gasps.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Right now.
